prerequisites: Prerequisites enforced by the course of study
Basic knowledge of the theory of physics and of electric circuits

learning_outcomes.text: Deep knowledge and understanding of the fundamental theoretical and practical aspects related to smart grid planning and management.
Capability to design the architecture of an intelligent management system of energy networks according to the paradigm of smart grids.
Capability to independently evaluate and choose enabling technology solutions to achieve intelligent management goals.
Capability to communicate technical information both orally and in writing.
Ability to discuss problems and solutions with specialists and non-specialists about the planning, design and operation of modern distribution systems.
Capability of continuous learning through the proper interpretation of scientific and technical literature, manuals of manufacturers and technical standards.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the course: electrical power systems
Fundamentals on power systems: transmission, distribution systems and final use of electricity
Main components of electrical systems (transformers, generators, lines and loads)
Fundamentals on operation and management of power systems (control and management systems, protection system, safety and reliability, electrical blackouts)
Evolution of energy systems
Enabling technologies and tools for the energy transition
Energy demand and energy systems
Conventional and renewable power plants
Study of the effects of the widespread use of network-connected distributed generation
The evolution of electricity demand
Connection rules of active and passive users
Integration of renewable and distributed resources in the electrical grid
Electrification of final consumption
The smart grid Definitions
Motivations for Smart grid
Smart grid architecture
Demand side management
Smart grid control and management systems (centralized, decentralized, hierarchical, etc.)
Telecommunications and digitization systems for smart grids
Protection systems for smart grids
Enabling technologies
Innovative operation schemes for future power systems (microgrids, energy communities, etc.)
Planning of smart grids
Overview of smart grid economics (regulation and market models)
teaching_methods: Notices on the teacher's web page

assessment_methods.method: Written intermediate tests with theoretical and practical questions
Oral test on the topics of the course

assessment_rules: The exam may consist of written intermediate tests and an oral test, or alternatively, only one oral test at the end of the course. Participation in intermediate tests is allowed only to students who regularly attend lessons. Not sufficient results in intermediate tests can be recovered at the final examination. A minimum grade of 18/30 is given for a basic level, and a maximum grade of 30/30 for outstanding results. For students who did not participate in tests, the final examination also includes specific written tests and exercises to assess applying knowledge and understanding skills.
